news.title: Vozinha: Cape Verde goalkeeper to join Chilean club Colo Colo after 2026 World Cup heroics
news.lede: 'He's the story' - Vozinha's goalkeeping heroics thwart Spain. Vozinha, the Cape Verde goalkeeper who earned plaudits for his World Cup performances, is set to join Chilean side Colo Colo. The 40-year-old headed to the World Cup without a club after his contract with Portuguese second division side Chaves expired, but he became an overnight sensation by starring in a goalless draw against eventual champions Spain. He has now found a new club, according to Colo Colo president Anibal Mosa.

news.title: Lionel Messi let himself down – failure to call out Argentina is an insult to football
news.lede: The South Americans were at the centre of various controversies during the tournament due to perceived over-physical tactics resulting in a number of tense confrontations. Argentina have long adopted football’s dark arts in a bid to gain a psychological advantage over their opponents. And that’s despite historically producing some of world football’s greatest-ever talents. Lionel Scaloni’s men were far from their best at the World Cup, often relying on the Messi's wizardry to pull themselves out of the mire.

news.title: Is it fair Argentina have an automatic spot in World Cup 2030?
news.lede: ARGENTINA have already secured their place in the 2030 World Cup after a never seen before Fifa decision to have six co-hosts. The team missed out on winning this year’s World Cup after a 1-0 extra time defeat to Spain – that was followed by an ugly brawl. But despite being condemned for the conduct, Argentina won’t have to go through the usual qualification campaign after Fifa‘s unheard of decision to have six co-hosts. The majority of the matches will be held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco but Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay are also set to have one match each on their shores.

news.title: World Cup hero Vozinha has a club but it is not Lionel Messi's Inter Miami
news.lede: After his unexpected yet magnificent World Cup heroics, Cape Verde's star, Vozinha now finally has a club! Josimar José Évora Dias, nicknamed Vozinha, has reached a verbal agreement with Chilean club Colo-Colo. Cape Verde's hero Vozinha to play for Chilean club Colo-ColoCape Verde played their first ever FIFA World Cup in 2026 and instantly became the story of the tournament, thanks to their incredible run. However, their main hero was Vozinha, who made his World Cup debut at 40 and took the football world by storm with his magnificent saves. .

news.title: Arsenal plot return dates for World Cup stars as one trains at former club
news.lede: Arsenal are readying for the return of several of their World Cup stars - but face decisions on how best to manage Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka . Several of the Gunners' players have been back as they're put through their paces, but the majority of their big-hitters were present at this summer's tournament. Those players are entitled to a minimum of three weeks off after their involvement for their countries. England stalwart Rice has been managing neural pain in his hamstring for more than six months.

news.title: How World Cup 2026 proved football has remarkable ability to cure all ills
news.lede: The trophy safely on display at the Spanish FA headquarters, England’s wounds no longer so raw, and the annual football calendar now into its miniscule vacuum, you’re left to reflect on the past six weeks and ponder whether the 2026 edition in the United States, Canada and Mexico was a resounding success or an unmitigated flop. This one really could have gone either way. The expansion from 32 teams to 48 had the potential for greater drama but also the risk of suffocating, of making the World Cup the one thing it should never be: tedious. Would North America buy into soccer in a way we hadn’t seen at USA 1994?

news.title: ‘It takes time’ — Dayot Upamecano’s journey to the top
news.lede: Bayern Munich and France men’s national defender Dayot Upamecano is a mainstay these days for club and country — an incredible feat, especially considering the talent available over the years to both sides. But he did not always look like a lock to be a lock in each team’s XI. Bayern fans will recall when Upamecano was the target of criticism following some Champions League exits earlier in his tenure. His time at France was not the smoothest sailing either, in the beginning.

news.title: Is There Really a Ballon d'Or Curse at the FIFA World Cup?
news.lede: Football's most prestigious individual award has often failed to translate into World Cup glory, with many Ballon d'Or winners falling short on the sport's biggest stage.
